review_summary: Question 8 (Magnetic Fields and Forces on Conductors) verified with PASS across all 3 leaves (a), (b)(i), and (b)(ii). Leaf (a) verifies the formal definition of magnetic flux density: force per unit current (B1) per unit length (B1) on a straight conductor placed normal/perpendicular to the magnetic field (B1). Leaf (b)(i) verifies the qualitative explanation for why current in arms PQ and RS does not disturb balance: using Fleming's left-hand rule, forces on PQ and RS act horizontally in the plane of the pivot and thus exert zero moment about the pivot (B1 + B1), or alternatively produce equal and opposite forces resulting in zero net force (B1 + B1). Leaf (b)(ii) verifies the calculation of flux density B using the principle of moments about the horizontal pivot: equating magnetic moment BILx to gravitational moment mgy (C1), substituting B * 2.7 * (1.2 * 10^-2) * (7.5 * 10^-2) = (45 * 10^-6) * 9.81 * (8.8 * 10^-2) (C1), and evaluating B = 1.6 * 10^-2 T (A1) with hybrid numeric checking at 0.016 T ± 0.001 T. All progressive hints, teacher walkthroughs, AI rubrics, deterministic checks, and taxonomy mappings are fully compliant.
